title: ASX secondary listing and updated marketing guidance
gist: Glencore replaces its fixed $2.3-3.5bn long-term Marketing Adj. EBIT guidance with a matrix tied to Readily Marketable Inventories and funding costs, implying a c.$3.5bn mid-point (c.$2.8-4.2bn) at June 2026 RMI of $32.2bn and ~5% funding cost, effective 2027. It also lifts FY2026 marketing EBIT expectations to above $5bn on reshaped oil, products, gas and freight markets, ahead of its ASX secondary listing (GLC) on 14 October 2026.

themes.theme: Marketing EBIT guidance reset via RMI/funding matrix

insights.claim: Glencore has replaced its fixed long-term Marketing Adjusted EBIT guidance range of $2.3bn-$3.5bn with a matrix methodology linking expected marketing EBIT to the level of Readily Marketable Inventories (RMI) and funding costs/interest rates.
insights.speaker: Glencore investor reports
insights.so_what: Guidance becomes a function of balance-sheet scale and rates, letting investors model trading earnings off RMI and SOFR rather than a static band.
insights.quote: incorporates, via a matrix, the interplay between funding costs and Readily Marketable Inventories (RMI), on expected Marketing Adj. EBIT outcomes

insights.claim: Glencore says its previous $2.3bn-$3.5bn marketing guidance reflected materially lower RMI levels and a lower interest-rate environment than today, implying the old range understated the trading arm's earnings capacity.
insights.speaker: Glencore investor reports
insights.so_what: Signals a structural upward rebase of the trading division's through-the-cycle earnings, supportive for valuation of the marketing business.
insights.quote: reflected materially lower RMI levels and an interest rate environment that has more recently broken to the upside

insights.claim: Applying the new matrix to 30 June 2026 RMI of $32.2bn and a marketing funding cost of about 5%, Glencore's long-term Marketing Adj. EBIT guidance mid-point would be about $3.5bn, within a range of about $2.8bn to $4.2bn.
insights.speaker: Glencore investor reports
insights.so_what: New mid-point equals the top of the old range, a ~20% lift versus the old ~$2.9bn mid-point.
insights.quote: the long-term Marketing Adj. EBIT guidance mid-point would be c.$3.5bn (range of c.$2.8bn to c.$4.2bn)

insights.claim: Glencore's RMI at 30 June 2025 was 21% lower at $25.4bn; with about $0.3bn lower associated funding costs, that would have mapped to a matrix guidance mid-point of about $3.2bn, showing sensitivity of roughly $0.3bn of guided EBIT to a ~$6.8bn RMI swing.
insights.speaker: Glencore investor reports
insights.so_what: Gives a rough sensitivity to model how guidance shifts as inventories and commodity prices move.
insights.quote: RMI at 30 June 2025 was 21% lower at $25.4bn

insights.claim: Glencore attributes the progressive, material rise in RMI over recent years mainly to commodity prices, inflation, the commercial opportunity set and growth in overall business volumes and scale.
insights.speaker: Glencore investor reports
insights.so_what: Higher commodity prices and inflation mechanically raise the guided trading earnings base under the new framework, making it partly pro-cyclical.
insights.quote: primarily due to movements in commodity prices, inflation, the commercial opportunity set and our overall business volumes and scale
insights.locator: RMI has moved progressively and materially

insights.claim: The matrix assumes a correlated relationship between RMI, funding costs/interest rates (referenced to 1-Month Term SOFR plus a margin) and marketing EBIT, effectively treating higher rates as something passed through into trading margins rather than a pure cost.
insights.speaker: Glencore investor reports
insights.so_what: Implies Glencore believes it can earn a return on working capital that rises with rates, a hedge against higher-for-longer interest rates.
insights.quote: an assumed correlated relationship with levels of RMI & funding costs/interest rates

insights.claim: Glencore defines RMI as core, liquid inventories readily convertible into cash whose price risk is primarily covered by forward physical sales or hedges, and says RMI ordinarily turns more than 10 times per year.
insights.speaker: Glencore investor reports
insights.so_what: Explains why RMI is treated as near-cash working capital and a scale driver of trading profit rather than price exposure.
insights.quote: RMI ordinarily turns >10 times per year

insights.claim: The new long-term marketing guidance methodology is intended to apply from 2027 onwards.
insights.speaker: Glencore investor reports
insights.so_what: 2027 consensus for marketing EBIT should be rebased to the matrix rather than the old band.

themes.theme: 2026 trading windfall from reshaped energy markets

insights.claim: Glencore now expects full-year 2026 Marketing Adj. EBIT to exceed $5bn, up from a 'mathematical' c.$4.9bn outcome flagged with H1 2026 results.
insights.speaker: Glencore investor reports
insights.so_what: An upgrade implying H2 2026 trading came in above the top end of prior guidance, a positive earnings revision.
insights.quote: We now expect full-year 2026 Marketing Adj. EBIT to exceed $5bn.

insights.claim: Glencore says its near-record H1 2026 marketing performance primarily reflected materially reshaped crude oil, refined products, gas and freight markets.
insights.speaker: Glencore investor reports
insights.so_what: Energy market dislocation is a key profit engine for commodity traders; volatility in oil, products, gas and shipping drives trader earnings.
insights.quote: primarily reflecting the materially reshaped crude oil, refined products, gas and freight markets

insights.claim: Glencore's 2026 marketing EBIT of over $5bn would be well above even the new long-term matrix range top of about $4.2bn, indicating 2026 is a cyclical peak-type year rather than the new normal.
insights.speaker: Glencore investor reports
insights.so_what: Investors should not extrapolate 2026 trading profits; normalized guidance is ~$3.5bn.

insights.claim: Glencore's ASX secondary listing under ticker GLC is expected to begin trading on Wednesday 14 October 2026, via CHESS Depositary Interests each representing one Glencore ordinary share.
insights.speaker: Glencore investor reports
insights.so_what: Opens access to Australian investors and index flows, potentially broadening the shareholder base.
insights.quote: Each Glencore CDI represents a beneficial interest in one Glencore ordinary share.

insights.claim: Holders of Glencore ordinary shares in the UK and South Africa can convert them into ASX-traded CDIs via Computershare, with South African conversions also subject to Exchange Control Regulations.
insights.speaker: Glencore investor reports
insights.so_what: Enables cross-listing arbitrage and liquidity migration between London, Johannesburg and Sydney lines.
